DOOM is from an era where story was superfluous. I don't give two shits about a story, characterization, resource management, player stats, or any of that nonsense. DOOM should be about shooting monsters and moving forward to find an exit. That's it. If you throw anything else into that mix it will detract from the experience.

I know of only one other PC game franchise that has duplicated that formula successfully--Serious Sam. If Croteam were making this new DOOM, I'd be really stoked. As it stands I'm skeptical that these new developers are going to try and add bullshit to the game to service younger gamers and/or console gamers.

There is no fair way to compare the two. Doom was a technological marvel in its day with years of fond memories, nostalgia and tributes to it and this is just another flashy fps. This game should be judged for its own merits, not compared to one of the fathers of the genre. It would be like judging Jimmy Carter poorly by comparing him to George Washington.

I sort of disagree with you. You shouldn't/can't just call a game "DOOM" because it's about a space marine killing demons. Game franchises normally stay true to specific genres and styles of gameplay. DOOM I & II had a specific style of gameplay that is no longer fashionable--i.e. "run & gun." Story, resource management, NPCs, etc. were of little importance (whereas in modern FPS' they are integral). The HUD was minimal and could be removed. Weapons didn't have alternate fire modes, and could be easily selected by hitting a button. What the player is left with is a streamlined gaming experience that is fast, visceral, and intuitive.

When you deviate from that streamlined gameplay, you fundamentally change the game. It would be like taking a Heavy Metal song and having a Disco artist record it. You might recognize certain elements, but it would be a pale (infuriating) imitation. And that's what the original DOOM gameplay pretty much was....Heavy Metal: fast, aggressive, violent. It was barebones and raw--containing only the essential elements--get from point A to point B and kill everything in between.

Any attempt to "modernize" DOOMs gameplay by adding in superfluous elements will be a disaster. And if they're developing it with an eye towards making it console-friendly then they should just call it anything but DOOM.
